article_title: Learning to Read in Chinese: A Meta-analytic Structural Equation Modeling Analysis of Cognitive-Linguistic Skills in Chinese Word Reading
citation: Learning to read in Chinese: A Meta-analytic Structural Equation Modeling analysis of cognitive-linguistic skills in Chinese word reading. (2025). https://osf.io/s7tjp/?view_only=4865c0558529407aa0a9e35777761117
title: Lexical Quality Hypothesis as a framework for cognitive-linguistic underpinnings of word reading
description: The article adopts the Lexical Quality Hypothesis (Perfetti, 2007) as its organizing theoretical framework, contending that "successful word reading depends on readers' high-quality orthographic representations, well-specified phonological representations, and rich and elaborated semantic representations" of a word. When these components are firmly connected, word reading becomes faster and more effortless, freeing resources for comprehension. The MASEM model operationalizes these representations as five cognitive-linguistic skills predicting word reading.
requirements: Models of word reading must include the covariance among skills and control for nonverbal reasoning to estimate each skill's unique effect, as the article argues univariate approaches obscured unique contributions
constraints: The framework is applied here to typically developing native Chinese-speaking children under age 18 in mainland China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong
target_learners: Native Chinese-speaking children (kindergarten through elementary school)
target_learning_goals: Word reading (character and multi-character word recognition) in Chinese
examples: The study fitted a path model in which RAN, OA, PA, MA, and vocabulary predicted word reading, testing the interplay the LQH implies
key_sources: Learning to read in Chinese: A Meta-analytic Structural Equation Modeling analysis of cognitive-linguistic skills in Chinese word reading. (2025). https://osf.io/s7tjp/?view_only=4865c0558529407aa0a9e35777761117

article_title: Human learning dynamics during teleoperation of surgical robots
citation: Yinqi Huang, Yilin Cai, Mengyao Li, Yue Chen & Robert C. Wilson. (2026). Human learning dynamics during teleoperation of surgical robots. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-026-00442-6
title: LQG controller with an updated internal motion-scaling estimate as a baseline model of human teleoperation learning
description: The article models the human teleoperator as a linear-quadratic-Gaussian (LQG) controller that "explicitly separates state estimation from feedback control" and carries "an internal estimate of the motion scaling ratio that is updated over training". The Kalman gain provides an interpretable parameter governing how internal state estimates are updated across training, retention, and transfer. Humans and the model showed qualitatively similar improvement and generalization patterns, so the authors position the model as "a baseline model for rail-tracking behavior, rather than as a full perceptual model of teleoperation".
requirements: System dynamics must be defined; the model targets continuous closed-loop sensorimotor control under sensory noise rather than reward-driven sequential decision problems.
constraints: The model does not incorporate strategic exploration, fatigue, or attention, and was given the rail centerline rather than stereo endoscopic visual feedback; it intentionally simplifies human kinematics and omits cognitive-load mechanisms.
target_learning_goals: motor skill acquisition and generalization in surgical robot teleoperation
examples: The controller was initialized with an incorrect motion-scaling estimate, completed 12 training trials in four blocks, and was tested on a transfer trial at g = 0.4, mirroring the human experiment.
key_sources: Yinqi Huang, Yilin Cai, Mengyao Li, Yue Chen & Robert C. Wilson. (2026). Human learning dynamics during teleoperation of surgical robots. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-026-00442-6

article_title: Progress in Teachers' Readiness to Promote Positive Youth Development among Students during the Lions Quest Teaching Workshop
citation: Talvio, M., Berg, M., Ketonen, E., Komulainen, E., & Lonka, K. (2015). Progress in Teachers’ Readiness to Promote Positive Youth Development among Students during the Lions Quest Teaching Workshop. Journal of Education and Training Studies, 3(6). https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v3i6.869
title: Measuring perceived importance, competence and task value provides a practical way to evaluate learning from short teacher workshops
description: The article proposes that evaluating teachers’ experienced importance, perceived competence and task value serves as a practical indicator of readiness to change following short professional development courses. The authors state that "Investigating perceived importance, competence and value allows us to investigate learning through short courses such as LQ relatively well." This approach extends the Kirkpatrick four-phase model by adding motivational perspectives beyond reactions and knowledge alone.
requirements: Data collection before and after the training using Likert-scale questionnaires measuring perceived importance, perceived competence and task value
constraints: The study did not investigate whether teachers subsequently implemented the skills they learned into practice
Implementation in the classroom relies on school policy and administration, not solely on workshop quality
target_learning_goals: Social and emotional learning (SEL) promotion skills
Readiness to apply training content in the classroom
examples: The study measured 153 Finnish teachers before and after a two-day LQ workshop using seven-point Likert scales, comparing gains against a first comparison group of 61 non-participating teachers and a second comparison group of 46 teachers
key_sources: Talvio, M., Berg, M., Ketonen, E., Komulainen, E., & Lonka, K. (2015). Progress in Teachers’ Readiness to Promote Positive Youth Development among Students during the Lions Quest Teaching Workshop. Journal of Education and Training Studies, 3(6). https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v3i6.869

article_title: Progress in Teachers' Readiness to Promote Positive Youth Development among Students during the Lions Quest Teaching Workshop
citation: Talvio, M., Berg, M., Ketonen, E., Komulainen, E., & Lonka, K. (2015). Progress in Teachers’ Readiness to Promote Positive Youth Development among Students during the Lions Quest Teaching Workshop. Journal of Education and Training Studies, 3(6). https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v3i6.869
title: Expectancy-value theory as a framework for understanding teacher motivation to attend and apply SEL training
description: The article applies expectancy-value theory (Eccles & Wigfield, 2002; Wigfield & Eccles, 2000) to explain teacher participation in and engagement with SEL training. According to the article, "expectancies and values influence one’s performance, such as through participation in an upcoming course." Expectancies for success evaluate perceived competence, while subjective task values consist of attainment value, intrinsic value, utility value and cost. The framework predicts that teachers who consider LQ content important and motivating are more likely to implement LQ skills in their own classroom.
requirements: Measurement of both expectancies (perceived competence) and subjective task values (attainment, intrinsic, utility value and cost)
target_learners: In-service teachers participating in continuing education
target_learning_goals: Willingness to apply learned SEL skills in the classroom
examples: The study measured task values consisting of attainment, intrinsic and utility values and cost among LQ workshop participants
